clue.text: Unsuccessful student making fresh start at Rugby

definitions.meaning: someone who abandons a course before finishing it
in rugby union, play restarts from the 22-metre line with a drop-kick of this name

explanation.surface: A failed pupil gets a second chance at Rugby, the famous English public school.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby with a capital looks like the school, but here it is the game, whose restart after a touchdown-in-goal is a drop kick of this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A student who leaves a course without completing it is commonly called this, hyphenated.

clue.text: It's not cheap, love!

definitions.meaning: a term of endearment, as in 'my love'

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both expensive and beloved, the second used as an affectionate form of address.

clue.text: Id est

parts.note: Latin for 'that is', but read as 'Ide is': the ide is another name for this freshwater fish

explanation.walkthrough: The Latin tag that gives us i.e. is reread as a statement that the ide (a carp-like fish) is the thing named.
explanation.definitionFit: The ide is a European freshwater fish also known by this name, the golden variety kept in ponds.

clue.text: Cursory examination not repeated

definitions.meaning: a quick inspection, a glance over something
done a single time and finished with, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a quick look, and read literally says something happened a single time and was done.

clue.text: Taking offence

definitions.meaning: the act of taking what belongs to another

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as the idiom 'taking offence', being upset, but the two words define separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing is both a taking of property and a criminal offence.

clue.text: Doesn't sound it, but it's hot

definitions.text: Doesn't sound it, but it's hot

parts.words: Doesn't sound it, but it's hot
parts.note: spoken, the word sounds like the adjective for cold, yet it names a fiery pepper

explanation.definitionFit: A chilli is a hot pepper, though its name is pronounced the same as the word meaning cold.

clue.text: The ore may be converted to this

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Raw ore might be processed into some product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be converted' rearranges THE ORE; the definition 'to this' borrows the 'to' that seems to belong to 'converted'.
explanation.definitionFit: The formal adverb means to this matter or document, as in 'attached hereto'.

clue.text: A pointless intrigue?

parts.note: in tennis a score of nil is called love, so an affair with no points is a romantic liaison

explanation.definitionFit: A romantic relationship, especially an illicit one, is a kind of intrigue; the tennis score for zero supplies the first word.

clue.text: Show it's all true, strangely enough

indicators.note: strangely signals that the letters are arranged in an odd new way

explanation.surface: Demonstrate that an unlikely claim is entirely accurate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely enough' rearranges ITSALLTRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To show something by example or picture is a synonym, as in 'show the point with a diagram'.

clue.text: Moved camp

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both emotionally touched and pretentiously artificial in manner.

clue.text: One who treats vile disorder and rot

parts.note: a doctor, abbreviated Dr, treats patients

indicators.note: disorder means jumbled, so the letters of vile are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor deals with some nasty illness and decay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rot' reads as decay but means nonsense; 'disorder' is the anagram signal for vile, giving IVEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Rot in the sense of nonsense talk is a synonym, as in 'what utter rot'.

clue.text: Exceptional talent may be hidden

indicators.note: read as out of the usual order, signalling the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's outstanding gift might go unnoticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exceptional' rearranges TALENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something present but not yet showing itself is hidden or dormant, a synonym.

clue.text: Chap splits drinks with us — bags of them

indicators.note: the chap breaks the pair of drinks apart, sitting between them

parts.note: port and tea are two drinks
a chap is a man
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man divides up drinks with others, carrying plenty of bags.
explanation.walkthrough: Two drinks are split by the chap; 'of them' only pads the surface, and the plural here is the anglicised one rather than the French -x.
explanation.definitionFit: Large travelling cases hinged to open in two halves are bags of this name.

clue.text: Soldiers embark in aircraft and ships

indicators.note: to embark in a craft is to go inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: fighters are military aircraft
RE, the Royal Engineers, is a common abbreviation for soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops board planes and vessels for deployment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embark in' is the container signal; the soldiers go in just after the first letter of the aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo vessels are ships, and the word covers cargo aircraft too.

clue.text: A way, and only one, to outclass all rivals

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
taken as written
alone means only one, solitary

explanation.surface: A method, and the single one, of beating all competitors.
explanation.definitionFit: To be unequalled is idiomatically to have no one standing beside you, beating every rival.

clue.text: Returns to digs for economy's sake

definitions.text: Returns to digs for economy's sake

parts.words: Returns to digs for economy's sake
parts.note: read as going back to the trenches, but meaning cuts back spending

explanation.definitionFit: To cut back expenses is to economise, and literally it suggests digging in again.

clue.text: Music provided by the strings for the audience

indicators.note: what an audience hears is the spoken sound, so the word is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: cords are strings

explanation.surface: A string section plays for the listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the audience' says CORDS is heard; 'Music' is the definition, with 'provided by the' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Groups of notes sounded together are an element of music, a looser sense than the musical term.

clue.text: Service return a good way out

indicators.note: return means go back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: In tennis, a return of service lands well wide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns RAF backwards; the surface is about tennis, but 'Service' is an armed service.
explanation.definitionFit: Something a long distance off is distant, a good way out.

clue.text: Sulky demeanour

definitions.meaning: a light two-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle, a sulky is an example of this
the way one holds oneself, bearing

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sulky' looks like a mood, but here it is a horse-drawn cart.
explanation.definitionFit: A sulky is a kind of horse-drawn vehicle, and one's bearing or deportment is also called this.

clue.text: It is charged for a portion without wine

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the wine is taken away from the word

parts.note: port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Someone pays extra for a serving of food with no wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes PORT from PORTION; 'charged' means carrying an electric charge, not billed.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom or molecule that carries an electric charge is the chemistry term in question.

clue.text: I'd return to break agreement in dispute

indicators.note: the piece breaks into the agreement, splitting it

parts.note: a contract is a formal agreement

indicators.note: return means go back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: I'd gives the letters ID

explanation.surface: Someone means to go back on a deal during an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses I'd to DI, and 'to break' is the container signal; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispute a statement is to deny it, a synonym.

clue.text: Many dwell on this anagram made by setter

indicators.note: the clue openly says the letters of the following word are rearranged

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of an anagram for where many people live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anagram made by' rearranges SETTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Many people live on a road in a town, so their address names it.

clue.text: Dear Sir, These could be what you've always wanted

indicators.note: could be signals the letters may be formed into something else

explanation.surface: A letter opens Dear Sir, and these things are your dearest wish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges DEARSIRTHESE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the thing someone longs for most of all.

clue.text: A sign of disunity in Croatia

definitions.meaning: a break or division between people
a port city on the Dalmatian coast of Croatia

explanation.definitionFit: A division is a sign of disunity, and the coastal city in Croatia shares the name.

clue.text: A girl artist has it framed

indicators.note: framed means surrounded, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is an artist
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter has a picture of a young woman framed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'framed' is the container signal and 'has' a link; RA stands for Royal Academician.
explanation.definitionFit: Rita is a girl's name, a crossword example of a girl.

clue.text: Extremely light

definitions.meaning: a ... light is a coloured flare fired from a pistol

explanation.walkthrough: A Very light, named after its inventor Edward Very, is a signal flare.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means extremely, and is also a signal flare named after its inventor.

clue.text: Took sweetheart and ran

parts.note: running away with a lover, typically to marry in secret

explanation.definitionFit: To run off secretly with a lover, usually to marry, is the meaning.

clue.text: Feel a bit irritated by a trifling annoyance

indicators.note: irritated suggests the letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: Feeling slightly vexed by a minor nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irritated' rearranges FEELABIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A small insect bite stands for any minor irritation or trivial nuisance.

clue.text: Bedclothes used as ropes

definitions.meaning: on a sailing boat, ... are ropes controlling the sails

explanation.walkthrough: Knotted bedsheets used as an escape rope is the surface image, but sailors call sail ropes sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names bed linen and also the lines used to trim a ship's sails.

clue.text: The charge incurred by you initially for treatment

parts.note: taken as written
a rap is a criminal charge, as in 'beat the rap'

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so take the first letter

explanation.surface: The fee you pay for medical care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the Y of 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: Treatment of illness or disorder, physical or mental, is a synonym.
